policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: ASV keeps the object ('to heal the sick') and the mapped note 'Some ancient authorities omit the sick' shows the omission is the note's reading, not the text's, so r01 is excluded; τοὺς ἀσθενεῖς and the participial τοὺς ἀσθενοῦντας both come into English as 'the sick'.
ASV reads the singular 'neither staff'; the plural ῥάβδους is rendered 'staves' where ASV has it (KJV's reading here), so the number in the English distinguishes the singular.
ASV 'neither have two coats' leaves the distributive untranslated; a suppressed ἀνά is ordinary ASV practice and does not show its absence from the text.
ἄν and ἐάν are orthographic variants of the same particle with the subjunctive; 'as many as receive you not' renders either.
Present δέχωνται and aorist δέξωνται both surface as the English present 'receive you not'; ASV does not mark subjunctive aspect here.
The added καί would join the participial clause to the imperative; ASV's comma ('when ye depart from that city, shake off') is the same rendering either conjunction receives.
Present imperative ἀποτινάσσετε and aorist ἀποτινάξατε are alike 'shake off' in ASV; imperative aspect is not distinguished in the English.
ASV reads 'heard of all that was done' with no agent; the RP addition ὑπ᾽ αὐτοῦ would give 'by him', which ASV renders wherever it stands.
Aorist ἠγέρθη and perfect ἐγήγερται both come into the reported clause as 'that John was risen from the dead'; the English tense follows the indirect discourse, not the Greek stem.
τις and εἷς alike yield 'one of the old prophets' in ASV; the indefinite and the numeral are not separated by this wording.
ASV 'And Herod said' renders either connective; ASV regularly gives δέ as 'And' when no contrast is drawn, so the English does not choose between εἶπεν δέ and Καὶ εἶπεν.
The variant is the article with the proper name Ἡρῴδης, which English does not represent; 'And Herod said' is compatible with either.
English requires the subject pronoun in 'about whom I hear such things' whether or not emphatic ἐγώ stands; ASV does not mark the emphasis.
ASV 'withdrew apart to a city called Bethsaida' matches πόλιν καλουμένην Βηθσαϊδά; the RP reading is 'a desert place of a city called Bethsaida', and ASV has no desert place here.
ASV 'he welcomed them' is a rendering either the compound ἀποδεξάμενος or the simplex δεξάμενος can carry; the English does not isolate the compound.
πορευθέντες and ἀπελθόντες are both 'that they may go into the villages'; ASV does not distinguish the two verbs of going here.
The variant is the article before ἀγρούς; 'the villages and country round about' reads the same with or without it.
Only the order of ὑμεῖς and φαγεῖν differs; English word order in 'Give ye them to eat' is fixed by its own syntax.
ἄρτοι πέντε and πέντε ἄρτοι are both 'five loaves' in English, which puts the numeral first regardless.
ASV reads 'about five thousand men'; the approximating ὡσεί is present in the English, and the RP text omits it.
κατέκλιναν and ἀνέκλιναν both come into ASV as 'made them all sit down' (Greek recline); the preverb is not distinguished.
Aorist παραθεῖναι and present παρατιθέναι are alike 'to set before the multitude'; infinitive aspect leaves no English trace.
Only the order of οἱ ὄχλοι and λέγουσιν differs; 'Who do the multitudes say that I am?' follows English interrogative order either way.
The readings differ in the order of Πέτρος and ἀποκριθείς and in the article; 'And Peter answering said' puts the subject first as English requires.
Present λέγειν and aorist εἰπεῖν are both 'to tell this to no man'; the infinitive's aspect is not rendered.
ASV reads the passive 'be raised up'; ἀναστῆναι is intransitive and ASV renders it 'rise again', so the passive in the English answers to ἐγερθῆναι.
r00-base and r01 differ only in punctuation, which no translation shows; and ἐλθεῖν/ἀπαρνησάσθω give the same 'would come after me, let him deny himself' as the base verbs.
ASV reads 'take up his cross daily'; καθ᾽ ἡμέραν stands in the English and the RP text omits it.
ἄν and ἐάν are orthographic variants of the same particle; 'whosoever would save his life' renders either.
Adverbial αὐτοῦ and ὧδε are both 'here' in 'some of them that stand here'; ASV does not separate them.
ἑστηκότων and ἑστώτων are alternate perfect participle forms of the same verb, both 'that stand'.
The resumptive καί after the temporal phrase is absorbed by the 'it came to pass ... that' construction; ASV shows no separate word for it.
The variant is the article with Πέτρος, which English does not represent; 'Peter said unto Jesus' is compatible with either.
Imperfect ἐπεσκίαζεν and aorist ἐπεσκίασεν both come into ASV as 'and overshadowed them' in the narrative chain.
αὐτούς and ἐκείνους are both the plain subject 'they' of the infinitive clause 'as they entered into the cloud'; order and pronoun choice leave no English difference.
ASV reads 'This is my Son, my chosen', rendering ἐκλελεγμένος, and the mapped note 'Many ancient authorities read my beloved Son' places ἀγαπητός in the margin.
The variant is the article before Ἰησοῦς; 'Jesus was found alone' reads the same with or without it.
ASV 'on the next day' renders the bare dative of time as readily as ἐν with the dative; the preposition leaves no separate English word.
ἐβόησεν and ἀνεβόησεν are both 'cried' in ASV; the preverb is not distinguished.
Only the order of μοι and ἐστίν differs; 'for he is mine only child' follows English order either way.
μόγις and μόλις are alternate spellings of the same adverb, both 'hardly' in 'it hardly departeth from him'.
Only the position of ὧδε differs; 'bring hither thy son' fixes the English order independently.
ASV reads 'all the things which he did' with a pronoun subject; the RP reading names ὁ Ἰησοῦς, which ASV renders 'Jesus' wherever it stands.
ASV reads 'when Jesus saw the reasoning of their heart'; 'saw' is the rendering of the aorist participle ἰδών, whereas εἰδώς is a verb of knowing and is given 'knowing' or 'perceiving' in ASV.
The variant is the case of παιδίον after ἐπιλαβόμενος; 'he took a little child' renders either construction.
ἄν and ἐάν are orthographic variants of the same particle; 'Whosoever shall receive this little child' renders either.
ἄν and ἐάν are orthographic variants of the same particle; 'whosoever shall receive me' renders either.
ASV reads the present 'the same is great'; the RP future ἔσται would give 'shall be great', which the English does not have.
The variant is the article with Ἰωάννης; 'And John answered and said' is the same either way.
ASV gives both ἐν and ἐπί with ὄνομα as 'in thy name' (compare 'in my name' in v. 48 for ἐπί); the preposition is not distinguished.
Imperfect ἐκωλύομεν and aorist ἐκωλύσαμεν both come into ASV as the past 'we forbade him'.
ASV reads 'But Jesus said unto him', drawing the contrast that renders δέ; 'But' is not a rendering of the RP's initial καί.
The variant is the article before Ἰησοῦς; 'Jesus said unto him' reads the same with or without it.
ASV reads 'not against you is for you', so the second person forms exclude RP's ἡμῶν … ἡμῶν; r00-base and r01 carry the same ὑμῶν … ὑμῶν and are not separated by the English.
ASV 'set his face' supplies the possessive from the article as it regularly does with body parts; 'his' does not show that αὐτοῦ stood in the text.
ἐστήρισεν and ἐστήριξεν are alternate aorist forms of the same verb, both 'stedfastly set'.
ASV renders the clause as a plain narrative sequence ('and they went, and entered'), representing neither ὡς nor ὥστε with a distinct word.
ASV 'his disciples James and John' supplies the possessive from the article in its usual way; 'his' does not show that αὐτοῦ stood in the text.
ASV ends the question at 'consume them?' and the mapped note reads 'Many ancient authorities add even as Elijah did', placing ὡς καὶ Ἠλίας ἐποίησεν in the margin.
ASV reads only 'But he turned, and rebuked them'; the mapped note assigns 'and said, Ye know not what manner of spirit ye are of' to some authorities, not to the text.

ASV reads only 'And they went to another village'; the note at v. 55 assigns 'For the Son of man came not to destroy men's lives but to save them' to fewer authorities, so the RP expansion is not in the text.
ASV reads 'And as they went on the way'; the RP Ἐγένετο δέ would give the 'And it came to pass' formula that ASV writes out wherever it stands (compare vv. 28, 33, 37).
ἐάν and ἄν are orthographic variants of the same particle; 'whithersoever thou goest' renders either.
ASV ends the man's words at 'whithersoever thou goest' with no vocative; the RP addition κύριε would give 'Lord', which ASV renders where it stands (as at v. 59).
ASV reads 'But he said, Lord, suffer me first'; the vocative Κύριε is in the English, and the WH text omits it.
Only the order of ἀπελθόντι and πρῶτον differs; 'suffer me first to go and bury my father' follows English order either way.
ASV reads 'But he said unto him' with a pronoun subject; the RP addition ὁ Ἰησοῦς would give 'Jesus', which ASV renders wherever it stands.
ASV reads 'But Jesus said unto him', so πρὸς αὐτόν is represented and r00-base, which lacks it, is excluded; r01 and r02 differ only in where πρὸς αὐτόν stands, which English order does not show.
ASV 'having put his hand to the plow' supplies the possessive from the article as it regularly does with body parts; 'his' does not show that αὐτοῦ stood in the text.
ASV 'is fit for the kingdom of God' renders the bare dative and εἰς with the accusative alike; the preposition is not distinguished.
